subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Self-Driving Cars: When Software Is the Engine
description: A short lesson to help you apply Self-Driving Cars: When Software Is the Engine.

hook.text: In 2004, DARPA held a race for self-driving cars. The best one made it 11 kilometers before crashing.

buildup.text: Self-driving cars use LIDAR, cameras, and radar to build a 3D map of their surroundings every 100 milliseconds.

discovery.text: The hardest problem isn't technology — it's predicting what a pedestrian will do next.

twist.text: Waymo's cars have driven 20 million miles. They crash less than humans — but each crash makes headlines.

climax.text: The trolley problem is no longer philosophy. Engineers must code who the car protects in a crash.

punchline.text: The hardest part isn't driving. It's deciding.

quiz.question: What is the hardest challenge for self-driving car engineers?
options: Building sensors accurate enough to see road markings
Predicting unpredictable human behavior on the road
Making batteries that last long enough for daily use
